report.source_text: Plain and contrast MRIs of the brain were requested, which revealed a heterogenous lobulated lesion in the region of the left side of the interpeduncular cistern extending to the prepontine cistern measuring 3 x 2.5 x 4 cm (Figures 1-3). A small component extended into the left cistern anterolateral to the pons in the left cerebellopontine angle. It was predominantly hyperintense on both the T1 weighted image (T1WI) and the T2 weighted image (T2WI), with some hypointense areas within, without significant enhancement (Figure 1, 2). Tiny T1 hyperintensities were seen diffusely scattered in subarachnoid spaces in the brain, likely to be fat (Figure 4). There was a mass effect on the left mid-brain and the left pons. Anteriorly, it abutted the left internal carotid artery. Restricted diffusion was seen (Figure 5).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old woman presented with acute left-sided vision loss, ptosis (decreased palpebral fissures), diplopia, and severe facial pain with touch-triggered attacks. Physical examination revealed the left eyeball directed downward and outward, consistent with cranial nerve involvement. MRI brain with contrast on admission revealed a 3 × 2.5 × 4 cm heterogenous lobulated lesion in the left interpeduncular and prepontine cisterns extending into the left cerebellopontine angle, with mass effect on the left midbrain and pons, abutting the left internal carotid artery, and showing restricted diffusion with scattered T1 hyperintensities consistent with fat—imaging findings highly consistent with a dermoid cyst. The clinical presentation of vision loss, ptosis, diplopia, and facial pain was explained by mass effect from the cyst compressing cranial nerves III, IV, VI (causing ocular motility deficit and ptosis), and V (causing trigeminal distribution facial pain). The patient underwent craniotomy with surgical removal of the dermoid cyst and irrigation of subarachnoid spaces to remove ruptured contents and debris, which was the definitive treatment for this lesion.
